The judge disclosed that his former chambers' service company was a party to a claim by the litigant in person, and resolved doubt in favour of recusal on apparent bias grounds. stories.ltme_summary: Above the Law carries a sponsored piece from Sensei Enterprises, a provider of IT, cybersecurity and forensics services, arguing that law firms need an AI strategy rather than more AI subscriptions. The article says adoption is spreading one tool at a time and sets out security questions firms should ask vendors, including training use, retention and access. It features a conversation with Trustpoint.One CEO Christopher Gallagher.

E-discovery is changing what lawyers ask and when they ask it
stories.ltme_summary: Canadian Lawyer reports that e-discovery is changing on authenticity and timing. Lawyers in Canada face deepfake risks, and Ontario's proposed AI evidence rules would presume some undisclosed AI-generated evidence inadmissible. The Civil Rules Review Working Group's December 2025 report proposes a reliance-based disclosure model. Several lawyers are quoted, including Emily Hazlett, Kelly Friedman and Kathryn Manning.

The item is a short summary only, so the amount and round stage rest on this single outlet line rather than a full article or company statement.

Henry joined Weil in 2024 from Willkie Farr & Gallagher. The article places the hire within Weil's proposed wind-down, which is dispersing partners and lawyers across the market.

The Financial Times reports the deal value at about €2.6bn, though the deal value is not officially disclosed. Carlyle and PAI say the business more than doubled its EBITDA since 2022.

The page records removals and updates to entries, including a 3 November 2026 removal of one provider's website after an error. The guidance says legal representatives must book with approved providers unless HMCTS agrees otherwise.

The founders also announced a $6.4m seed funding round. The extract is brief, so details of the product and investors are not available from it.
stories.hook: Former DOJ antitrust chiefs launch FluxCap agentic AI litigation platform with $6.4m seed round

The interview, recorded at Inspire in Orlando, also covers the legal context graph and a beta MCP connector with Legora. The text is the podcast summary, relayed in the company's own framing.

stories.title: Jus Mundi Adds AI-Powered Arbitrator Search to Jus AI
stories.ltme_summary: Legal Tech Monitor reports that Jus Mundi has added an AI-powered arbitrator search to its Jus AI product. stories.hook: Jus Mundi adds AI arbitrator search to Jus AI for shortlisting and researching candidates

stories.title: New York State Bar Association tells lawyers not to bill for time saved by AI
stories.ltme_summary: The New York State Bar Association's Committee on Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technologies has issued a report, adopted by the governing body, on billing for AI. Per Law360, the report treats AI software costs as overhead that can be passed on as a disbursement only when tied to a specific client matter and disclosed. Lawyers need not tell clients about AI use for purely administrative tasks, provided fees are unaffected. NYSBA president Taa Grays says the guidance is meant to help attorneys use AI ethically.
stories.hook: New York State Bar says AI software costs can be passed to clients only when tied to a specific matter and disclosed

stories.title: Connecticut’s AI Rules Take Shape: What Employers and Developers Need to Know // Cooley // Global Law Firm
stories.ltme_summary: Cooley analyses Connecticut's SB 5, signed on 27 May 2026 as Public Act 26-15, focusing on employment-related AI rules. Employer disclosure and notice duties start on 1 October 2027, and the attorney general enforces them with no private right of action. The alert flags that the 'materially influence' test may be broader than New York City's law.
stories.hook: Cooley says Connecticut's SB 5 covers AI tools that merely inform employment decisions from October 2027

Pao, Tracy Rubin, Sean Quinn and Brian Nelson have written an article for Law360 on the legal and operational risks of deploying open-weight AI models. It covers licensing, intellectual property, privacy and cybersecurity, and includes a pre-deployment checklist. The item is a relayed law firm thought piece.
stories.hook: Cooley partners set out a pre-deployment checklist for open-weight AI risks in a Law360 article

stories.title: FCA Enforcement Monthly | Morrison Foerster
stories.ltme_summary: Morrison Foerster's monthly False Claims Act newsletter covers Medicare Advantage chart-review settlements, including Independence Blue Cross paying $22.5m, and DOJ's opioid pharmacy cases, including CVS paying $315m.

stories.title: UK judge elected to international court
stories.ltme_summary: Professor Dapo Akande, a fellow of All Souls College, Oxford, has been elected a judge of the International Court of Justice after a vote by UN Member States, according to Solicitors Journal. The article says he will serve a nine-year term and that the election marks the return of a UK judge to the court after almost a decade. It quotes the Prime Minister and the Foreign Secretary welcoming the result.
stories.hook: Professor Dapo Akande elected to the International Court of Justice, restoring a UK judge after a decade

stories.title: Is it time to reform legal services regulation?
stories.ltme_summary: Solicitors Journal publishes a commentary arguing that gaps in the statutory framework for legal services regulation are now exposed. It cites the High Court ruling in Carter-Ruck that the SRA cannot compel privileged material without client consent, now subject to a leapfrog appeal to the Supreme Court, and the Court of Appeal's Mazur decision on conduct of litigation. The author, who acted for the Law Society in Mazur, calls for reform.
stories.hook: A Solicitors Journal commentary argues Carter-Ruck and Mazur expose gaps in the Legal Services Act framework

stories.ltme_summary: Docusign has published part three of a series on how it processes contracts at scale, explaining how custom extractions reach the accuracy of its standard models without training a new model for each field.

stories.title: Preservation, Proportionality, Privilege, and Prompts: The 13th Annual Judicial Panel | Relativity Blog | Relativity
stories.ltme_summary: Relativity's blog reports on its 13th Annual Judicial Panel at RelFest, with five judges from federal, state and England and Wales courts. The panel discussed AI hallucinations, citing Damien Charlotin's tracker, which the blog says has risen from over 400 cases in October 2025 to 2,262. Judges offered views on candour, the scale of the problem and AI use.
stories.hook: Relativity's judicial panel says AI hallucination cases have reached 2,262, though one judge calls the count misleading

stories.title: Law Firm Data Is Valuable. Now It Might Come With a Price Tag
stories.ltme_summary: Legal Tech Monitor reports that at least two AI-native law firms have bid for data belonging to Weil, Gotshal & Manges. The piece raises whether internal law firm data counts as an asset that an outside buyer can acquire. The extract is brief and does not name the bidders.
stories.hook: Two AI-native firms bid for Weil Gotshal's data, testing whether internal law firm data can be sold

stories.title: Illinois Supreme Court Amends Rule 10-101 Standardized Court Forms, Addressing Unauthorized Practice of Law Concerns
stories.ltme_summary: The Illinois Supreme Court amended Rule 10-101 on standardised court forms, effective 15 October 2026, clarifying that providing forms is not unauthorised practice of law.

stories.title: Close Calls: An Interactive Look at the Redgrave Study: Artificial Intelligence Trends
stories.ltme_summary: Doug Austin on eDiscovery Today describes a Relativity interactive game built on the Redgrave study of aiR Review. Players classify ten close-call documents from a 45,004-document Mallinckrodt set and compare their calls with four teams. The author reports he matched the aiR team on eight of ten documents and notes only two documents drew unanimous classification.
stories.hook: Relativity's Close Calls game lets reviewers test their document calls against the Redgrave aiR Review study

stories.title: The Jumpstart Outline from The Sedona Conference: eDiscovery Best Practices
stories.ltme_summary: Doug Austin reports that The Sedona Conference's Working Group 1 has published a new draft of the Jumpstart Outline for member and public comment. The 32-page update covers AI, generative AI and newer data sources. Comments are open until 11 December 2026, and the final version is due in January 2027.
stories.hook: Sedona Conference opens comment on a 32-page Jumpstart Outline update covering generative AI until 11 December

stories.title: 9 Tips and Questions to Ask When Choosing an eDiscovery Vendor: eDiscovery Best Practices
stories.ltme_summary: Doug Austin on eDiscovery Today republishes a sponsored guest post from Nextpoint on choosing an eDiscovery vendor. The post cites ILTA's 2026 Technology Survey, which reports 94 per cent of firms using or exploring generative AI, and 8am's finding that most firms lack formal AI policies. Nextpoint is disclosed as an Educational Partner and sponsor of the blog.
stories.hook: Nextpoint sponsored post on choosing an eDiscovery vendor cites 94 per cent of firms exploring generative AI

stories.title: The practical guide to Data Subject Access Requests
stories.ltme_summary: Mishcon de Reya has published a practical guide to data subject access requests (DSARs). The firm describes DSARs as a significant compliance and operational challenge for organisations. The extract is a short summary, so the guide's detailed steps and recommendations are not covered here.
stories.hook: Mishcon de Reya offers a practical guide to handling data subject access requests

A Brief History of Generative Legal AI
stories.ltme_summary: Artificial Lawyer founder Richard Tromans charts the rapid growth of generative legal AI since 2022. He cites OpenAI, Google, Anthropic and Microsoft entering legal, Harvey's valuation above $15 billion, and Legora's total investment above $1.4 billion. He also notes a rise in AI-native law firms, and promotes the Legal Innovators UK and New York conferences.
stories.hook: Artificial Lawyer's Richard Tromans traces a shift from Casetext to four tech giants entering legal AI in three years

stories.title: AI Law Firms Circle What Is Left of Weil Gotshal
stories.ltme_summary: LawFuel reports that AI-native firms are circling the remains of Weil, Gotshal & Manges. Scissero has expressed interest in Weil's technology, IP and data, Crosby has bid for its trademark and data, and Vetta wants precedents and lawyers. The piece cites an $85m raise at Crosby and a $10m bid for airline data as a benchmark, and says no asset transfer has been announced.
stories.hook: Scissero, Crosby and Vetta circle Weil's remains, but none of the expressions of interest is an announced transfer

The move follows Weil's proposed wind-down, announced on 28 October, and comes a week after Gibson Dunn hired Weil's London funds team of nearly 40 lawyers. Partners are reported to be leaving across the market.

Huge increase in complaints about barristers’ social media posts
stories.ltme_summary: Legal Cheek reports that complaints to the Bar Standards Board about barristers' social media posts more than doubled, from 132 to 279, in 2025-26, according to the regulator's annual report. Most related to the Israel-Palestine conflict. The BSB also concluded 114 investigations, with 51 per cent referred for disciplinary action. Phil Golding, the BSB's director general, cited operational pressure.
stories.hook: Bar Standards Board social media complaints against barristers rise from 132 to 279

stories.title: Is Google becoming pay-to-play for law firms?
stories.ltme_summary: Legal Futures publishes a sponsored commentary by Stacey Horrocks of BSD Legal Marketing on how Google search has changed for law firms. It notes expanded paid placement, the April 2025 auction change and the October 2025 'Sponsored results' grouping. The author argues rankings no longer equal visibility and that firms should track enquiries from search.
stories.hook: BSD Legal Marketing's Stacey Horrocks argues a first organic ranking no longer guarantees law firm visibility on Google

stories.title: SRA “keeping close eye” on accumulator law firms
stories.hook: The SRA says it now reviews accumulator firms monthly and widens its definition to two or more acquisitions in 24 months

stories.title: AI-native US firm opening in London as part of global expansion
stories.ltme_summary: Legal Futures reports that Manifest OS, a US AI-native immigration business, has made its first UK hire, Sophy King, as president of international immigration. The company plans to expand to more than 100 jurisdictions and open 40 offices within a year, starting with a London office. The UK operation would be regulated by the Immigration Advice Authority, according to King.
stories.hook: Manifest OS names Sophy King to lead international immigration as it plans 100 jurisdictions and 40 offices

stories.title: Trainee solicitor and paralegal banned for sexual offences convictions
stories.ltme_summary: Legal Futures reports that the SRA has made section 43 orders barring a trainee solicitor at Southampton University's legal services department and a former Ramsdens paralegal from working in SRA-regulated practice without approval. Both were convicted of sexual offences involving children, and the SRA says the convictions make their involvement in legal practice undesirable.
stories.hook: SRA bars a Southampton trainee and a former Ramsdens paralegal after child sexual offence convictions

stories.title: Dismay over government response to MPs’ legal aid report
stories.ltme_summary: Four legal advice charities have expressed dismay after the government did not accept any of the 28 recommendations in the justice select committee's report on legal aid. The committee said it interpreted the government as having rejected or declined to comment on all of them. The Ministry of Justice called the system inherited in crisis and cited extra funding figures.
stories.hook: Government accepts none of 28 justice committee legal aid recommendations, charities say
stories.amount: £116m per year criminal legal aid solicitors; £34m per year advocates; £20m per year civil

stories.title: Moore Barlow sale to Fletchers driven by “need to invest in technology”
stories.ltme_summary: Legal IT Insider reports that the sale of Moore Barlow to Fletchers was driven by a need to invest in technology. The extract is a site verification page only, so the buyer's reasoning and the deal terms are not set out here. It is a companion story to coverage of Knights' acquisition of part of the same firm.
stories.hook: Legal IT Insider links the Moore Barlow sale to Fletchers with a need to invest in technology

stories.title: Widespread redundancies follow Knights’ acquisition of 70% of Moore Barlow’s business
stories.ltme_summary: Legal IT Insider reports that widespread redundancies have followed Knights' acquisition of around 70 per cent of the business of Moore Barlow. The extract is a site verification page only, so the scale of job losses and the deal terms are not confirmed here. The piece is a sister story to coverage of the Fletchers sale of Moore Barlow, and the two should be read together for the transaction details.
stories.hook: Knights' takeover of 70 per cent of Moore Barlow is followed by widespread redundancies, according to Legal IT Insider

'Retraumatised': Grieving father received court bundle evening before inquest
stories.ltme_summary: The Law Society Gazette reports that Johnny Santer, an unrepresented father, received a disclosure bundle at 7.30pm the evening before his son's inquest, told the House of Commons justice select committee. INQUEST's Deborah Coles said the government has yet to decide the trigger point for legal aid for inquests under Hillsborough law.
stories.hook: Unrepresented father got inquest disclosure the night before hearing, telling MPs of legal aid trigger point delay
entities: House of Commons justice select committee

stories.title: Solicitors invited to contribute to review of police accountability
stories.ltme_summary: The Law Society Gazette reports that solicitors and others are invited to submit evidence to the review of police accountability, which runs to 15 January 2027. IOPC figures show more than 108,000 police complaints in 2025/26, up 15 per cent, though the IOPC says recording changes contributed. Co-chairs Dame Lynne Owens and Jason Beer KC are quoted.
stories.hook: Gazette urges solicitors to respond to police accountability review as complaints rise 15 per cent to over 108,000

stories.title: CPS cited non-existent authority in rape prosecution
stories.ltme_summary: The Law Society Gazette reports a High Court judgment in LYC v DPP in which the CPS cited a non-existent authority, R v J [2024] EWCA Crim 3529, in a written record for a prosecution. The court found the citation unsatisfactory but held it did not affect the outcome, refused permission to amend and dismissed the judicial review. The claimant was 14 and the alleged offence occurred when he was 11.
stories.hook: High Court says CPS fake citation did not affect rape prosecution decision and dismisses judicial review

stories.title: Personal injury heavyweights swallow up more of the claims sector
stories.ltme_summary: Express Solicitors has bought Ralli Ltd, a Sale-based personal injury firm with around 40 staff, according to The Law Society Gazette. Ralli's accounts for the year to June 2025 show pre-tax profit of £391,000 on revenue of about £3.8m. Express says it now has more than 1,000 staff and turnover of £65m for the year to August 2025.
stories.hook: Express Solicitors buys Ralli, with around 40 staff, in latest personal injury consolidation

stories.title: Legal academic elected as first UK International Court of Justice judge in a decade
stories.ltme_summary: The Law Society Gazette reports that Professor Dapo Akande has been elected to the International Court of Justice, the first British judge in a decade. He will serve nine years. The UK prime minister and foreign secretary welcomed the result, and the election also filled seats for France, Jordan, Singapore and Kenya.
stories.hook: Professor Dapo Akande elected to the International Court of Justice as the UK's first judge since 2017

stories.title: Weil trainees rescued as Gibson Dunn prepares to hire dozens of lawyers
stories.ltme_summary: The Law Society Gazette reports that Latham & Watkins has hired five trainees from the collapsing Weil, Gotshal & Manges London office, and that Gibson Dunn is expected to complete the hire of around 120 Weil private funds lawyers, including over 20 partners. Weil's leaders have recommended an orderly wind-down, according to the Gazette.
stories.hook: Latham takes five Weil London trainees as Gibson Dunn nears a 120-lawyer private funds hire

stories.title: His Master's voice: Sir Geoffrey Vos's greatest hits
stories.ltme_summary: Outgoing Master of the Rolls Sir Geoffrey Vos's six years in office are reviewed against his technology predictions, from 2018 forecasts on digital evidence to his views on AI in judicial decision-making.

stories.title: Mrs Justice Joanna Smith appointed Deputy President of the Business and Property Division
Independent study on the impact of age assurance on fundamental rights and costs for businesses
stories.ltme_summary: The European Commission publishes an independent study on age assurance, covering its effects on fundamental rights and costs for businesses, including small firms. The study was carried out by an external contractor and was commissioned to inform the proposed EU KIDS Act. It finds costs are likely to remain modest, and it highlights the EU age verification blueprint as a potentially affordable route for providers.
stories.hook: Commission study finds EU age verification blueprint could be one of the most affordable routes for service providers

stories.title: Call for evidence on advertising repositories
stories.ltme_summary: The European Commission is seeking feedback through a call for evidence on forthcoming guidelines for advertising repositories under the Digital Services Act. The guidelines will cover searchability, targeting insights and accessibility of ads on very large platforms and search engines. A targeted public consultation follows in 2027, with publication planned for the second quarter of 2028.
stories.hook: Commission opens call for evidence on DSA advertising repository guidelines, with publication planned for Q2 2028

stories.title: Police accountability
stories.ltme_summary: The Home Office secretariat is seeking views and evidence for the independent end-to-end review of the police accountability system. The review is chaired by Dame Lynne Owens and Jason Beer KC. The call for evidence closes at 11.59pm on 15 January 2027 and is separate from a Ministry of Justice consultation on the standard of proof for unlawful killing conclusions.
stories.hook: Police accountability review calls for evidence until 15 January 2027, chaired by Dame Lynne Owens and Jason Beer KC
